But, I just want to throw this monkey into the wrench: WWI had an entirely different kind of warfare. Cannonades, and random artillery bombarding the enemy without direct targeting. Mass-annihilation, with no real care for residual contact. WWII began the war of attrition, and snipers. individual kills, and they were rewarded. Fast forward and each war / conflict has become more personal. more individually targeted.

Over the years war has become a method of dispatch. Air and artillery forces are a discrete and precise weapon. They are no longer the blunt object of mayhem in wars past. Soldier on soldier combat is more common in most modern major conflicts. When it happens there is a different mindset, and the killing of an enemy is very personal. That is what has to happened in modern warfare starting in Vietnam.

This changes the idea of being a random target to being a person. You individually are targeted. You individually are targeting another human. That's intense. The "enemy" is XXX country / civilization, but the person you are in a fight with is an individual.

The reason of change is the directness of conflict, and the change of overall war strategies. In WWI I would be terrified if I could be randomly blow up from a lobbed explosive. WWII I would be terrified if some sniper picked me out on the beach. Korea I would be terrified if I was picked to be the public example or a bomb. Vietnam I would be terrified if I walked into an ambush trap. Fast forward to today. It is now a man-on-man war for every individual involved.

Imagine walking out of your bedroom every day expecting to fight for your life. That's a messed up mindset that can't easily be changed, especially considering the age of the individuals.
